title: The truth does not need a majority to be true.
subtitle: Why most people saying no changes nothing
then: The surah opens with letters whose meaning is known to Allah, a signal to stop and listen. Then it says plainly: {idea}what was sent to you is the truth.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ had been calling people for years, and {trap}most still refused{/trap}.
now: You post something you care about and get three likes. Your friends all skip the prayer, so you start to wonder if you are the odd one. The room goes quiet when you say you do not drink. {idea}A crowd can be loud and still be wrong.{/idea}
old: If most people do not believe it, maybe it is not that convincing.
new: The truth stays true even when most people walk past it.
try: Next time you feel like the only one doing something good, pause and say: I do this for my Lord, not the count.

title: A sky without pillars, so be sure of the meeting.
subtitle: Why the sky and sun point to the Day

row.title: evidence
sub: He who began it can return it

then: Ibn Kathir explains the verse as Allah showing His full power: the sky held up {idea}without pillars, as you see{/idea}, the sun and moon running for a term. The point is stated at the end: these signs are laid out so you become {reward}certain you will meet your Lord{/reward}.
now: You check the sunrise time on your phone for Fajr and it is right to the minute. Nobody holds the sky up, nobody winds the moon. You trust that schedule without thinking. {idea}The same Lord keeps the appointment with you.{/idea}
old: The sky and the sun are just background to my day.
new: The order up there is a promise that the meeting down the line is real.
try: Look up at the sky once today for ten seconds and remember you will meet the One who holds it.

title: Mountains, rivers, pairs of fruit, night over day: think.
subtitle: Signs that only open for people who reflect
then: After the heavens, the verse turns to the earth. Ibn Kathir describes it spread wide, with mountains, rivers, and {idea}every fruit in two kinds{/idea}, and day and night pursuing each other. Allah controls time as He controls space. But the verse says these are signs {reward}for people who think{/reward}.
now: You eat a mango in a hurry, standing at the counter, eyes on a screen. You drive past hills every day and have not seen them in months. Night falls and you only notice the battery percentage. {idea}The signs are there. The thinking is the missing part.{/idea}
old: I know nature is amazing, I do not need to think about it.
new: A sign only works on me when I actually stop and think about it.
try: Eat one piece of fruit today slowly, with the phone away, and notice it.

title: Same water, same soil, different fruit.
subtitle: Neighbouring plots that turn out completely different
then: Ibn Kathir explains the neighbouring tracts: some fertile, some {trap}dead and salty{/trap}, right next to each other. Vines, crops, palms, some from one root and some not, all {idea}watered with the same water{/idea}. Yet the taste, colour and scent differ. The verse calls this a sign for people who use reason.
now: Two siblings, same house, same parents, same school. One turns out gentle, one turns out sharp. Two coworkers get the same training and one shines. You keep asking why. {idea}Same water, different fruit. Someone decides the yield.{/idea}
old: If the inputs are the same, the results should be the same.
new: Even identical conditions give different fruit, and that difference points to Him.
try: Think of someone who started with the same as you and ended up differently. Make one kind dua for them.

title: The strange thing is doubting the second creation.
subtitle: They accept the first creation and deny the return
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the people denying resurrection already admitted that Allah created everything from nothing. Yet they said {trap}when we are dust, will we be made new?{/trap} The verse tells the Prophet ﷺ: if you want something to wonder at, wonder at that. {idea}The One who began it is more able to repeat it.{/idea}
now: You believe your body was built from a single cell, which is a miracle. Then you hear about rising again and something in you shrugs: sounds far-fetched. {idea}You already believe the harder thing.{/idea} The return is the easier one.
old: Coming back after death is hard to picture, so I keep it at a distance.
new: I already exist from nothing. Coming back is the smaller step.
try: Tonight, before sleep, remember sleep is a small rehearsal of the return, and thank Allah for waking you this morning.

title: They asked for the punishment while forgiveness was open.
subtitle: Hurrying the bad when the good is offered
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the disbelievers mocked by asking the Prophet ﷺ to {trap}bring the punishment now{/trap}, even though past nations had already been made examples. Allah answers that He is {reward}full of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing{/reward}, and also severe in penalty, so fear and hope are both held.
now: You say, half joking, if it is a sin, why has nothing happened to me? The delay feels like proof. It is not. {reward}It is time given to come back.{/reward} The door is open, and it will not stay open forever.
old: Nothing bad has happened, so maybe it does not matter.
new: The delay is His forgiveness giving me room, not proof that it is fine.
try: Pick one wrong you keep repeating and ask Allah's forgiveness for it today, by name.

title: You are a warner, not a miracle machine.
subtitle: Every people gets a guide; results belong to Allah
then: Ibn Kathir notes that the idolaters asked the Prophet ﷺ to {trap}turn the hill of Safa into gold{/trap} and move the mountains away. The reply: you are only a warner. {idea}Guidance is not your burden{/idea}, and every people has had someone calling them.
now: Your brother stopped praying and you have sent him every reminder clip there is. You lie awake running the next argument. {idea}Your part is to say it well and with love.{/idea} The heart is not in your hands.
old: If they do not change, it means I did not find the right words.
new: My job is to convey kindly. Changing hearts is Allah's.
try: Think of the person you most want to guide. Make dua for them instead of planning your next argument.

title: He knows what every womb holds, and everything has a measure.
subtitle: Knowledge of the unseen, down to the womb

row.title: Allah knows
sub: the term, the provision, the end

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah knows all that is in the wombs, and Ibn Abbas said {trap}what falls short{/trap} refers to miscarriage and what exceeds to the full term. When one of the Prophet's ﷺ daughters sent word that her child was dying, he replied that {idea}everything with Him has a fixed term{/idea} and she should be patient.
now: A hospital corridor. The doctor says there is no heartbeat. Or the due date passes and everyone keeps asking. You want someone to say why. {idea}Nothing in that womb was unseen or unmeasured.{/idea} He knew it before you did.
old: What happened in that pregnancy was random and out of everyone's hands.
new: It was out of my hands, but never out of His knowledge or His measure.
try: If you or someone close has lost a child, send them one gentle message today, with no advice in it.

title: Seen or unseen, He knows it, and He is greater.
subtitle: Four names that close the passage on His knowledge
then: Right after the womb, the verse widens the circle. Ibn Kathir explains He knows {idea}everything servants see and everything they cannot{/idea}, and none of it escapes Him. He is {reward}greater than everything and above everything{/reward}.
now: You have the version of you people see at work and the version alone at 1am. You manage both carefully. {idea}One Lord sees both, and is bigger than both.{/idea} That is a weight and a relief at once.
old: There is a part of me no one will ever really see.
new: He sees all of me, and He is still greater than all my worries.
try: Say Allahu Akbar slowly once today while thinking of the thing that feels biggest to you.

title: Whisper or shout, night or day: all the same to Him.
subtitle: No difference between your secret and your public
then: Ibn Kathir explains His knowledge covers those who {idea}hide their speech and those who declare it{/idea}. Aishah said she could not hear all of a woman who came complaining about her husband in the same room, yet {reward}Allah heard her and sent down verses{/reward} about it.
now: The voice note you deleted before sending. The muttering under your breath in the car. The private browser tab. The quiet complaint you have never told anyone. {reward}He heard the complaint too{/reward}, not only the sins.
old: What I keep quiet stays between me and no one.
new: My quietest words reach Him, including the ones I need Him to hear.
try: Tell Allah, in your own words and quietly, one worry you have told no one.

title: He will not change your state until you change yourself.
subtitle: Guarding angels, and the change that starts inside
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {reward}angels take turns guarding each person{/reward}, gathering at Fajr and Asr. Then the verse warns: Allah does not take away a people's good condition {idea}until they change what is in themselves{/idea}, turning from obedience to disobedience.
now: You keep saying things will get better once the new job comes, or the move happens, or the kids are older. Meanwhile the habits stay the same. {idea}The outside follows the inside.{/idea} And while you work on it, you are guarded more than you know.
old: My situation has to change before I can.
new: The change Allah gives starts with the change I make inside.
try: Pick one small habit that drags you down and replace it for one day only.

title: Lightning brings fear and hope in the same flash.
subtitle: One sign, two feelings, heavy clouds behind it

row.title: fear
sub: for the traveller on the road

row.title: hope
sub: for the farmer waiting for rain

then: Qatadah, quoted by Ibn Kathir, said the lightning is {trap}fear for travellers{/trap} who dread its harm, and {reward}hope for residents{/reward} who wait for its rain. The same flash means different things depending on where you stand. Both come from Him.
now: A storm while you are stuck on the motorway, wipers going, heart racing. Your cousin back home is praying for rain for the crops. {idea}Same sky.{/idea} Fear and hope are both reasons to turn to Him.
old: Storms are just weather, nothing to do with me.
new: Every flash is a reminder to fear Him and hope in Him at the same time.
try: Next time you see lightning or hear thunder, stop talking for a moment and remember Allah.

title: Even the thunder praises Him while people argue about Him.
subtitle: The sky glorifies; some on earth dispute
then: Ibn Kathir reports that Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr would {idea}stop talking when he heard thunder{/idea} and praise the One the thunder glorifies, calling it a stern warning to the people of earth. He also narrates the story of two men in Madinah who {trap}plotted against the Prophet ﷺ{/trap}; one was later struck by a thunderbolt.
now: Thunder rolls and you keep scrolling, or you joke about it in the family group. Everything in the sky is praising while you are mid-argument about something small. {idea}Stopping is the right response.{/idea}
old: Thunder is loud weather, that is all.
new: The thunder is praising Allah. The least I can do is go quiet and join it.
try: The next time it thunders, pause what you are saying and say SubhanAllah.

title: Calling others is like begging water to jump into your mouth.
subtitle: The only call that gets an answer

row.title: a thirsty man
sub: at the edge of a well

then: Ali ibn Abi Talib, quoted by Ibn Kathir, described a man {trap}stretching his hand at the edge of a deep well{/trap}, his hands not reaching the water, so how could it reach his mouth? That is calling on anything besides Allah. Ibn Abbas said {idea}the call of truth is la ilaha illallah{/idea}.
now: Late at night you refresh the inbox, hoping a reply from someone will fix your mood. You count on a boss, a lucky break, a person who keeps not showing up. {trap}Hands out over a well.{/trap} The One who actually answers is closer.
old: If I just get the right person on my side, I will be okay.
new: Only a call to Allah reaches. Everything else is hands over a well.
try: Before you message someone for help today, make a short dua to Allah first.

title: Everything bows to Allah, even your shadow.
subtitle: Willing or not, all creation submits
then: The surah keeps showing the people of Makkah signs of Allah's power. Here it says {idea}everything in the heavens and earth prostrates to Him{/idea}. Believers do it willingly. Those who refuse are still subject to Him, and even their shadows lean and stretch through the day.
now: Walk outside at eight in the morning and your shadow is long beside you. At four in the afternoon it falls the other way. You did not plan either. {idea}Your body already follows His order.{/idea} The only question left is whether your heart joins it.
old: I am free to live as if no one is in charge.
new: Everything already bows to Allah; I get to choose to bow willingly.
try: Next time you see your shadow, let it remind you to make one sincere sajdah today.

title: Why lean on helpers who cannot even help themselves?
subtitle: The Creator versus things that create nothing
then: The idol worshippers of Makkah admitted Allah made the heavens and earth. Ibn Kathir notes they even said in their pilgrim chant that He owned their other gods. Still {trap}they turned to those gods for help{/trap}. The verse asks: {idea}did your gods create anything like His creation?{/idea}
now: The bill is due and your first thought is the friend with money, then the boss, then luck. You check your horoscope app out of habit. None of these made the sky or keep your heart beating. {trap}They need help themselves.{/trap}
old: I believe in Allah, but in real life I lean on whatever seems useful.
new: If He alone created everything, He is the one to turn to first.
try: Before you ask any person for help with your next problem, ask Allah first in one short dua.

title: Foam rises fast and vanishes; what helps people stays.
subtitle: Two parables of truth and falsehood

row.title: what benefits
sub: water, gold, stays in the earth

then: Ibn Kathir explains two parables. Rain fills valleys, each by its size, as hearts hold knowledge by their capacity. {trap}Foam rises on the flood and on melted metal, then scatters.{/trap} {idea}The water and the metal remain.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said the foam is doubt and what remains is certainty.
now: A rumour trends for two days, then nobody remembers it. A loud opinion gets a million views and is forgotten by Friday. The quiet teacher who explained things kindly is still remembered years later. {reward}What actually helps people stays.{/reward}
old: Whatever is loudest and on top right now must be winning.
new: Falsehood is foam: it rises fast and has nothing under it.
try: Choose one small useful thing to do today that nobody will see, like teaching or fixing something.

title: Answering His call now is worth more than the whole earth later.
subtitle: Two responses, two endings

key.label: The offer that comes too late

then: After the parable of foam, the verse names the outcome. {reward}Those who answered their Lord get the best reward.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says those who refused would, on that Day, offer the earth full of gold and more to save themselves, and {trap}it would not be accepted{/trap}.
now: The adhan goes off on your phone while you are mid-scroll. A small voice says pray now, and another says in a minute. That small moment of answering is cheap today. {idea}Later, nothing you own could buy it back.{/idea}
old: I will answer Allah's call properly once life settles down.
new: The response is easy now and priceless later; today is the time to answer.
try: Next adhan you hear today, stop what you are doing within one minute and go pray.

title: Knowing the truth and being blind to it are not the same.
subtitle: Who actually takes the reminder
then: The verse asks if a person who knows the revelation to the Prophet ﷺ is true can be like a blind person. Ibn Kathir says they are never equal. {idea}Only people of sound understanding take the reminder{/idea}, and he adds a prayer: we ask Allah to make us among them.
now: Two people sit in the same Friday khutbah. One scrolls under the table. The other walks out thinking about one sentence for the rest of the day. {idea}Same words, different hearts.{/idea}
old: Hearing the Quran is enough; the rest will happen on its own.
new: The reminder works on those who stop and think about it.
try: Pick one verse you heard this week and spend two minutes thinking about what it asks of you.

title: People of understanding keep their word.
subtitle: The first mark: promises kept
then: This begins a list of the qualities of those who earn the good home. The first is {idea}keeping the covenant with Allah and not breaking it{/idea}. Ibn Kathir contrasts them with the hypocrite, who {trap}breaks a promise when he makes one and betrays when trusted{/trap}.
now: You told your mother you would call on Sunday. You told a coworker you would send the file by five. You told Allah, in a hard week, that you would pray on time. {reward}Small promises kept are how trust is built.{/reward}
old: A promise is a nice intention; plans change.
new: Keeping my word, to Allah and to people, is part of my faith.
try: Think of one promise you made and forgot. Keep it today, or tell the person honestly.

title: They keep joined what Allah wants joined.
subtitle: Family ties and a watchful heart
then: The list continues. Ibn Kathir says these people {idea}are good to relatives and do not sever kinship{/idea}, and are kind to the poor. They remember Allah is watching in what they do and say, and {trap}they fear a hard reckoning{/trap}.
now: The family group chat has gone quiet since the argument at the wedding. Your cousin has not called in two years, and neither have you. {idea}One message can rejoin what pride has cut.{/idea}
old: If they stopped calling, it is not my job to reach out.
new: Keeping family ties is an order from Allah, not a reward for good behavior.
try: Send one short, warm message today to a relative you have drifted from.

title: They answer harm with good.
subtitle: Patience, prayer, giving, and a gentle reply

row.title: evil for evil
sub: you hurt me, I hurt you

then: Ibn Kathir explains each habit. Their patience is for Allah's pleasure, not for show. They pray with care and give in every condition, by night and day. {idea}When people harm them, they answer with patience, pardon and forgiveness.{/idea} {reward}For such people there is a good end.{/reward}
now: A driver cuts you off and gestures. A sibling says something sharp at dinner. Someone leaves a nasty comment on your post. Your thumb is ready to reply. {idea}A calm, kind answer is the harder and better move.{/idea}
old: If someone is rude to me, they deserve the same back.
new: Meeting harm with good is a sign of the people Allah praises.
try: The next time someone is short with you today, answer with one kind sentence instead.

title: Paradise is not lonely; your righteous family comes too.
subtitle: Gardens of Eden and a reunion
then: Ibn Kathir says 'Adn means a lasting home. {reward}Allah gathers believers with their righteous parents, spouses and children{/reward} so their eyes are comforted, and raises the lower ones to join the higher. {idea}Angels come to them from every gate.{/idea}
now: You stand at a grave of a grandparent and wonder if you will ever see them again. You worry about your children growing up away from faith. {reward}The promise is a reunion{/reward}, and your own effort can be part of the bridge.
old: Whatever happens after death, I face it alone.
new: Allah can gather the righteous of a family together in Paradise.
try: Make dua today, by name, for a parent, spouse or child to be with you in Jannah.

title: Peace upon you, for what you patiently endured.
subtitle: The angels name the reason for the reward
then: The angels greet the people of Paradise. Ibn Kathir cites a hadith in Ahmad about poor emigrants who {trap}died with needs still in their chests{/trap}. {reward}Allah sends angels to greet them with Salam from every gate.{/reward} The reward names their patience.
now: The hospital corridor at two in the morning. The job you keep showing up to though it drains you. The prayer you make while nothing seems to change. {idea}None of that patience is lost.{/idea} It is the very thing the angels will mention.
old: My struggles are just bad luck I have to get through.
new: Patient endurance is what the angels will greet me for.
try: Name one thing you are enduring right now and tell Allah you are being patient for Him.

title: Breaking promises and cutting ties is the opposite road.
subtitle: The mirror image of the believers' qualities
then: Ibn Kathir says this verse is the exact opposite of the qualities just listed. Where the believers kept their word and family ties, {trap}these broke their covenant, cut ties and spread harm{/trap}. He cites the hadith on the signs of a hypocrite: lying, breaking promises, betraying trust.
now: It rarely starts big. One broken promise to a friend. One ignored call from a parent. One story passed on that you knew was untrue. {idea}Habits form a road, and roads lead somewhere.{/idea}
old: Little broken promises and family fallouts are just part of life.
new: These small breaks are the opposite of the believers' road; I can turn back.
try: Look at the two lists in verses 20 to 25 and pick one quality to move toward this week.

title: More money is not proof that Allah is pleased.
subtitle: Provision is a test, and this life is small
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah widens and narrows provision by His wisdom. {trap}Those who rejoiced in wealth did not realize they were being tested.{/trap} He cites a hadith in Muslim: {idea}this world beside the Hereafter is like the water on a finger dipped in the sea.{/idea}
now: Payday comes and the account looks good, and you feel like life is on your side. A friend's business fails and you quietly assume he did something wrong. {idea}Both are tests, not report cards.{/idea}
old: If I have more, Allah must be happier with me.
new: Rich or tight, it is a test, and this life is tiny next to the next.
try: Next time you check your bank balance, say Alhamdulillah and remember it is a test, not a grade.

title: Miracles do not guide; turning back to Allah does.
subtitle: The demand for a sign, and the real door
then: Ibn Kathir reports a hadith that the idolaters asked for Mount Safa to become gold. Allah offered the Prophet ﷺ their request, or {reward}an open door of repentance and mercy{/reward}, and he chose the door of mercy. {idea}Guidance is not tied to miracles; Allah guides those who turn to Him.{/idea}
now: You catch yourself thinking: if only I got a clear sign, I would change. If this job comes through, I will start praying. {idea}The sign you wait for is not the key.{/idea} Turning toward Him is, and that door is already open.
old: If Allah showed me something undeniable, I would finally change.
new: Guidance comes to whoever turns back to Allah, sign or no sign.
try: Stop waiting for a sign. Make one small turn toward Allah today, like two rakahs of sincere prayer.

title: Hearts find rest in remembering Allah.
subtitle: Where a restless heart settles

row.title: the next thing
sub: one more scroll, one more buy

then: Right after saying Allah guides those who turn to Him, the verse describes them. Ibn Kathir says {reward}their hearts become calm when Allah is remembered{/reward}, pleased to have Him as Protector and Supporter. {idea}He is worthy of it.{/idea}
now: It is late, you are anxious, and you have refreshed the same app ten times. Nothing settles. {idea}Put the phone face down and say SubhanAllah slowly, ten times.{/idea} Notice your breathing change.
old: When I am anxious, I need a distraction.
new: My heart is made to settle when it remembers Allah.
try: Tonight before sleep, sit for two minutes with no phone and quietly remember Allah.

title: Faith plus good deeds: Tuba and a beautiful return.
subtitle: What belief and action together earn
then: Ibn Kathir lists what the early scholars said Tuba means: {reward}happiness, comfort, joy, an excellent thing earned{/reward}, all meaning the same. He also cites a hadith about a vast tree in Paradise called Tuba. {idea}It is promised to those who believe and act on it.{/idea}
now: You feel your faith on a quiet night, then the next morning you snap at your kids and skip Fajr. {idea}Belief that rests the heart wants hands that work.{/idea} The happiness promised grows from both.
old: As long as my heart believes, what I do matters less.
new: Real faith shows up as good deeds, and the two together earn Tuba.
try: Turn one thing you believe into one small action today, like a kind word or a coin for charity.

title: He is my Lord, I rely on Him, I turn to Him.
subtitle: The Prophet's answer to people rejecting the Most Merciful
then: The Prophet ﷺ was sent like messengers before him, who were also rejected. Ibn Kathir notes the Quraysh {trap}disliked the name Ar-Rahman{/trap}, and at Hudaybiyyah refused to write it. The reply is calm: {idea}He is my Lord, in Him I trust, to Him I return.{/idea}
now: Your coworkers joke about religion at lunch, and you feel the heat rise. You could argue, or go silent and ashamed. {idea}There is a third way: quiet certainty.{/idea} He is my Lord, I rely on Him. Nothing more needs proving.
old: When people reject my faith, I have to win the argument.
new: I can state who my Lord is, trust Him, and leave it there.
try: Memorise the last line of this verse and say it to yourself the next time faith feels awkward in public.

title: If any book could move mountains, it is this one.
subtitle: The Quran is the miracle, and the decision is Allah's
then: The idolaters kept asking for spectacular signs. Ibn Kathir says if any scripture could move mountains or make the dead speak, {idea}it would be this Quran{/idea}. He cites a hadith that every prophet had a miracle that ended with him, but {reward}the Quran remains for all time{/reward}.
now: You want people you love to believe, and you think: if I just found the perfect video or argument. You send link after link. {idea}The strongest proof already exists, and still guidance is Allah's to give.{/idea} Your job is to share it gently.
old: If I find the right proof, they will have to believe.
new: Nothing is stronger than the Quran, and guidance still belongs to Allah.
try: Instead of arguing with someone today, make a quiet dua for their guidance by name.

title: Mockery is old; so is the respite before the reckoning.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ in the face of ridicule
then: Allah comforts the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}messengers before you were mocked too.{/idea} Those who mocked were given time, then taken. Ibn Kathir cites a hadith in Bukhari and Muslim: {trap}Allah gives the wrongdoer respite, and when He seizes him, He does not let go.{/trap}
now: You have been getting away with something for months: a habit, a lie at work, a harsh tone at home. Nothing bad has happened, so it feels fine. {idea}Respite is not approval. It is time to fix it.{/idea}
old: If nothing bad has happened yet, it must not be that serious.
new: Delay is a mercy and a warning; it is my window to turn back.
try: Name one wrong you have been getting away with, and take one step to stop it today.

title: The One watching every soul is not like a name.
subtitle: Name your partners, if they are real

row.title: show of words
sub: a plan made to look good

row.title: name them
sub: if real, He would know them

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah watches every soul, and {idea}nothing escapes His knowledge{/idea}. The idols could not hear, see or help. So the verse says: name them. If they existed, He would know. {trap}Their own scheming was made to look attractive to them{/trap}, and it blocked them from the path.
now: You say you trust Allah, but your stomach is tied to the stock app, the approval of your in-laws, the follower count. Ask honestly: {idea}what are these, really, next to the One who knows every soul?{/idea}
old: These things I worry about have real power over my life.
new: Only Allah stands over every soul; the rest are just names I gave power.
try: Write down the one thing you check most anxiously. Before checking it next time, say: Allah knows.

title: No one can shield a person from Allah.
subtitle: Hardship here, and heavier after, for rejection
then: After describing their rejection, the verse names the cost. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {trap}the punishment of this world is lighter than that of the Hereafter.{/trap} This world's pain ends. {idea}No one can defend a person against Allah.{/idea}
now: You fear embarrassment, a bad review, a fine, being found out. You rarely fear what lasts. {idea}Weigh your choices against the meeting with Allah, not just the reaction of people.{/idea} And His door is still open.
old: What I really need to avoid is trouble in this life.
new: The consequence that matters most is with Allah, and I can still turn to Him.
try: Before one decision today, ask: how will this look before Allah, not just before people?

title: A garden whose fruit and shade never run out.
subtitle: What the God-conscious are promised
then: Right after the warning, the promise. Ibn Kathir says the rivers flow wherever its people wish, and {reward}its food, fruit and drink never end{/reward}. {idea}This is the end of those who are mindful of Allah.{/idea}
now: The fridge empties by Thursday. The summer shade moves off your balcony by noon. The best meal of your life is gone in twenty minutes. {reward}Imagine nothing good ever running out.{/reward}
old: Every good thing ends, so grab it while it lasts.
new: There is a home where good things last, and mindfulness of Allah leads there.
try: Next time you enjoy a good meal or shade today, pause and ask Allah for the lasting one.

title: Worship Allah alone: invite to Him, return to Him.
subtitle: Some rejoiced, some rejected part; the message stayed simple

row.title: invite to Him
sub: and to Him is my return

then: Ibn Kathir says some People of the Book {reward}rejoiced at the Quran{/reward}, because their own books spoke of it. Others accepted some and rejected some. The Prophet ﷺ is told to keep the message simple: {idea}worship Allah alone, call to Him, return to Him.{/idea}
now: You like the parts of faith that feel easy and quietly skip the parts that ask more of you. Prayer yes, honesty in the tax form maybe. {idea}The message is whole, and it is simple: Him alone.{/idea}
old: I can keep the parts of the deen that suit me.
new: The core is simple and whole: worship Allah alone and walk back to Him.
try: Name one teaching you have been quietly skipping, and take one small step toward it.

title: Knowledge received is not to be traded for opinions.
subtitle: Following desires after guidance has come
then: Allah sent the Quran as {idea}a clear judgement in Arabic{/idea}. Then a warning addressed to the Prophet ﷺ himself. Ibn Kathir says it {trap}warns people of knowledge against following misguidance after knowing the truth{/trap}.
now: You know what is right about the deal at work, but the whole office does it the other way and it is easier to go along. {idea}Knowing is a responsibility.{/idea} Once you know, the crowd's opinion is no cover.
old: If everyone around me does it, I can follow them.
new: Once I know the truth, following others' desires leaves me unprotected.
try: Pick one thing you already know is right and act on it today, even if no one else does.

title: Messengers were human, with families, and signs came by Allah's leave.
subtitle: Why a prophet eats, marries, and waits
then: The idolaters objected that the Prophet ﷺ was an ordinary man. Ibn Kathir says {idea}all the messengers were human, with wives and children{/idea}. He cites the hadith: I fast and break fast, pray at night and sleep, and marry. {idea}No messenger brought a sign except by Allah's permission.{/idea}
now: You think real devotion means leaving normal life: no marriage, no job, no laughter. Then you feel like a fraud for enjoying dinner with family. {idea}The best of people lived full human lives.{/idea}
old: Being truly religious means stepping away from ordinary life.
new: Faith is lived inside family, work and ordinary days, like the messengers did.
try: Do one ordinary thing today, like eating with family, with the intention of following the Sunnah.

title: Allah erases what He wills and confirms what He wills.
subtitle: Why dua is never wasted
then: Ibn Kathir reports that Abu Wa'il, and similar from Umar and Ibn Mas'ud, used to pray: {reward}if You wrote us among the wretched, write us among the blessed{/reward}, for You blot out and confirm what You will. He cites a hadith in Ahmad: {idea}nothing turns back decree except dua.{/idea}
now: The scan results come back bad. The visa is refused. You think: it is written, nothing to do. {reward}Raise your hands anyway.{/reward} The One who holds the master book invites you to ask Him.
old: Everything is already decided, so my prayers change nothing.
new: Allah blots out and confirms what He wills, and He told me to ask.
try: Tonight, make the dua of the early Muslims: O Allah, write me among the blessed.

title: Your job is to convey; the results are Allah's.
subtitle: Whether or not you see the outcome
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: whether We show you some of what We promised them, or take you before that, {idea}your duty is only to convey{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says by conveying he fulfils his mission, and {idea}the reckoning is on Allah{/idea}.
now: You keep reminding your teenage son to pray, and nothing changes. You start to feel you have failed as a parent. {reward}Your part is to convey with love.{/reward} The heart is in Allah's hand, not yours.
old: If they do not change, I have failed.
new: My task is to convey well; the outcome belongs to Allah.
try: Give one gentle reminder today, then let go of how it lands.

title: No one can overturn Allah's decision.
subtitle: The ground shifting, and the swift reckoning
then: Ibn Abbas understood this as Allah granting the Prophet ﷺ land after land, while the idolaters felt secure. Ibn Kathir links it to towns destroyed around them. {idea}Allah judges, and no one can reverse His judgement.{/idea}
now: Your health, your savings, your position at work feel solid until one phone call. Things that seemed permanent shrink at the edges. {idea}Only His decision stays.{/idea} Lean on Him, not on what feels fixed.
old: What I have built is secure.
new: Everything shifts except Allah's judgement, so my trust belongs with Him.
try: Thank Allah today for one thing you usually treat as permanent.

title: They plotted, but all planning belongs to Allah.
subtitle: Who gets the good end
then: Ibn Kathir says people before them {trap}plotted to drive the messengers out{/trap}, but Allah planned against them. {idea}He knows what every soul earns.{/idea} {reward}The followers of the messengers get the good end{/reward}, in this life and the next.
now: Someone at work is quietly working against you, taking credit, whispering to the manager. You lie awake planning a counter-move. {idea}You are not the only planner in this room.{/idea} Stay honest; Allah sees all of it.
old: If I do not out-plot them, they will win.
new: All planning is Allah's; I just need to stay on the honest path.
try: Next time you feel schemed against, say Hasbiyallah and choose the honest action.

title: Allah is witness enough.
subtitle: When people say you are not who you say
then: The surah ends where it began, with rejection. The disbelievers say: you are not a messenger. The answer: {idea}Allah is enough as a witness{/idea}, and so are those with knowledge of scripture. Ibn Kathir says these are the scholars of earlier scripture who {reward}found his description in their books{/reward}.
now: Someone spreads a story that you are not sincere. Your family doubts your intentions. You want to post a long defence. {idea}Allah saw what you did and why.{/idea} His witness is enough.
old: I need people to believe me to be at peace.
new: Allah knows the truth about me, and that is enough.
try: Next time you are misjudged, skip the long defence and say quietly: Allah is my witness.
